nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-02.title: Altitude via Heron's formula
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-02.body:
Since $D$ lies on the circle with diameter $AB$, $\angle ADB=90^\circ$, so $AD$ is the altitude from $A$ to $BC$. By Heron's formula with $s=9$, the area is $\sqrt{9\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2}=6\sqrt6$. Then $\frac12\cdot 6\cdot AD=6\sqrt6$ gives $AD=2\sqrt6$, and in right triangle $ABD$, $BD=\sqrt{25-24}=1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-02.title: Law of Cosines
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-02.body:
$\angle ADB=90^\circ$, so $BD=AB\cos B$. By the Law of Cosines, $\cos B=\frac{5^2+6^2-7^2}{2\cdot5\cdot6}=\frac{12}{60}=\frac15$. Hence $BD=5\cdot\frac15=1$.

**Answer: 1**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-03.title: Multiply the remaining fractions
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-03.body:
Each discount leaves a fraction of the price: $25\%$ off leaves $\frac34$, $20\%$ off leaves $\frac45$, $37\frac12\%$ off leaves $\frac58$, $33\frac13\%$ off leaves $\frac23$. The final price is $\frac34\cdot\frac45\cdot\frac58\cdot\frac23=\frac14$ of the original, which is a single discount of $75\%$.

**Answer: 75**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-03.title: Try a price
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-03.body:
Start with \$120. After $25\%$ off: \$90; after $20\%$ off: \$72; after $37\frac12\%$ off: \$45; after $33\frac13\%$ off: \$30. The total drop is \$90 out of \$120, i.e. $75\%$.

**Answer: 75**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-04.title: Only squares have an odd number of divisors
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-04.body:
Divisors of $n$ pair up as $d \leftrightarrow n/d$; a divisor is paired with itself only when $d^2=n$. So $n$ has an odd number of divisors exactly when $n$ is a perfect square. The three-digit squares are $10^2,11^2,\dots,31^2=961$, which is $22$ numbers. Of the $900$ three-digit numbers, $900-22=878$ have an even number of divisors.

**Answer: 878**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-05.title: Inclusion–exclusion
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-05.body:
Squares below $2014$: $1^2,\dots,44^2=1936$, so $44$. Cubes: $1^3,\dots,12^3=1728$, so $12$. Both (sixth powers): $1,64,729$, so $3$. Squares or cubes: $44+12-3=53$. Of the $2013$ positive integers below $2014$, $2013-53=1960$ are neither.

**Answer: 1960**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-06.title: Add 1 and factor
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-06.body:
Adding $1$ to each equation gives $(x+1)(y+1)=20$, $(y+1)(z+1)=30$, $(x+1)(z+1)=54$. Multiplying, $\big[(x+1)(y+1)(z+1)\big]^2=32400$, and since all factors are positive, $(x+1)(y+1)(z+1)=180$. Dividing by each equation: $z+1=9$, $x+1=6$, $y+1=\frac{10}{3}$. So $(x,y,z)=\left(5,\frac73,8\right)$.

**Answer: $\left(5,\frac73,8\right)$**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-06.title: Substitute
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-06.body:
Let $X=x+1$, $Y=y+1$, $Z=z+1$, so $XY=20$, $YZ=30$, $XZ=54$. Then $\frac{XZ}{YZ}=\frac{X}{Y}=\frac{54}{30}=\frac95$, so $X=\frac95Y$ and $\frac95Y^2=20$, giving $Y^2=\frac{100}{9}$, $Y=\frac{10}{3}$. Then $X=6$, $Z=9$, so $(x,y,z)=\left(5,\frac73,8\right)$. Check: $5\cdot\frac73+5+\frac73=19$.

**Answer: $\left(5,\frac73,8\right)$**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-07.title: Intersecting chords
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-07.body:
Inscribe the pentagon in a circle; each side cuts off an arc of $72^\circ$. The angle between two intersecting chords equals half the sum of the intercepted arcs. $\angle CPE$ intercepts arc $CE$ (through $D$, $144^\circ$) and arc $AB$ ($72^\circ$), so $\angle CPE=\frac12(144^\circ+72^\circ)=108^\circ$.

**Answer: 108**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-07.title: Angle chasing
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-07.body:
Each interior angle is $108^\circ$. Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with apex $B$, so $\angle BAC=36^\circ$; similarly $\angle ABE=36^\circ$. In triangle $ABP$, $\angle APB=180^\circ-36^\circ-36^\circ=108^\circ$, and $\angle CPE$ is vertical to $\angle APB$, so it is also $108^\circ$.

**Answer: 108**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-10.title: Complementary counting
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-10.body:
There are $3^5=243$ strings in all. Strings with no A: $2^5=32$; with no B: $32$; with neither (all C): $1$. So $32+32-1=63$ strings miss an A or a B, leaving $243-63=180$.

**Answer: 180**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-10.title: Count by letters used
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-10.body:
Strings using exactly A and B: $2^5-2=30$. Strings using all three letters: $3^5-3\cdot2^5+3=150$. Total $30+150=180$.

**Answer: 180**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-11.title: Inner cube
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-11.body:
The unpainted cubes are those not on the surface; they form an inner cube with edge $6-2=4$, so there are $4^3=64$.

**Answer: 64**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-12.title: Quadratic in one variable
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-12.body:
Let the numbers be $x,y$ with $x+y=n$, a positive integer. Then $x^2+(n-x)^2=2$, so $2x^2-2nx+n^2-2=0$ and $x=\frac{n\pm\sqrt{4-n^2}}{2}$. For real values $n\le2$; $n=2$ gives $x=y=1$, not distinct. So $n=1$ and the numbers are $\frac{1\pm\sqrt3}{2}$. The greater is $\frac{1+\sqrt3}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1+\sqrt3}{2}$**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-12.title: Use the product
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-12.body:
With $x+y=n$, $xy=\frac{n^2-2}{2}$. Distinct real roots of $t^2-nt+xy=0$ need $n^2-4xy=4-n^2>0$, so $n=1$ and $xy=-\frac12$. Then $t^2-t-\frac12=0$ gives $t=\frac{1\pm\sqrt3}{2}$; the greater is $\frac{1+\sqrt3}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1+\sqrt3}{2}$**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-14.title: Centroid splits the area
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-14.body:
$G$ is the centroid, so $AG=2\,DG$ and $[ABD]=3[BDG]$; since $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $[ABC]=2[ABD]=6[BDG]$. Triangle $BDG$ is isosceles with $BG=BD=6$ and base $DG=2$; its altitude from $B$ bisects $DG$ and has length $\sqrt{36-1}=\sqrt{35}$. So $[BDG]=\frac12\cdot2\cdot\sqrt{35}=\sqrt{35}$ and $[ABC]=6\sqrt{35}$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt{35}$**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-14.title: Heron's formula
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-14.body:
Triangle $BDG$ has sides $6,6,2$, $s=7$, area $\sqrt{7\cdot1\cdot1\cdot5}=\sqrt{35}$. The three medians cut a triangle into six triangles of equal area, and $BDG$ is one of them, so $[ABC]=6\sqrt{35}$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt{35}$**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-16.title: Checkerboard coloring
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-16.body:
Color the board like a checkerboard. Each move changes color, so a path through all $36$ squares (an even number) alternates colors and ends on the opposite color from its start. But opposite corners of a $6\times6$ board have the same color. So no winning path exists.

**Answer: 0**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-17.title: Choose values and positions
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-17.body:
Pick the repeated value ($10$ ways), the other value ($9$ ways), and the position of the single value ($3$ ways): $10\cdot9\cdot3=270$.

**Answer: 270**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-17.title: Complement
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-17.body:
There are $10^3=1000$ triples; $10$ have all three equal and $10\cdot9\cdot8=720$ have all different. So $1000-10-720=270$ have exactly two equal.

**Answer: 270**

nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-18.title: Distances in the plane
nyciml-2014-15-fall-junior-18.body:
$\sqrt{x^2+9}$ is the distance from $(0,0)$ to $(x,3)$, and $\sqrt{(x-11)^2+16}$ is the distance from $(x,3)$ to $(11,7)$. The total is at least the straight-line distance from $(0,0)$ to $(11,7)$, which is $\sqrt{121+49}=\sqrt{170}$; equality holds when $(x,3)$ is on that segment, at $x=\frac{33}{7}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{170}$**
